newsitem.title: USA: RJR domestic tobacco volume dips, intl rises.
newsitem.headline: RJR domestic tobacco volume dips, intl rises.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp said Tuesday fourth quarter domestic tobacco volume was down three percent and international volume up 10 percent, while worldwide tobacco volume was up five percent.

In the international tobacco business, net sales totaled $1.01 billion in the fourth quarter, a 19 percent increase over the 1995 quarter. The company said the operating contribution of $227 million rose 10 percent, excluding one-time restructuring expenses.
For the full year, international tobacco net sales grew 12 percent, while the operating company contribution excluding one-time restructuring expenses and volume both increased by 10 percent.
The company said it was now in a position to "deliver attractive earnings in 1997" as a result of investments it has been making in tobacco marketplace programs.
Earlier, the company reported fourth quarter net of $248 million, or $0.73 a share versus $207 million, or $0.60 a share, excluding one-time items in both years.

The items excluded are one-time expenses of $33 million aftertax, or $0.10 a fully diluted common share, from a restructuring program. The 1995 quarter excludes aftertax expense of $163 million, or $0.49 a share filly duluted, from reorganization of the tobacco business.
The results were slightly higher than the First Call consensus estimate of $0.71 a share.
After the opening, the company's stock was trading at 32-5/8, up 3/8.
